term: per accidens (accidentally) ordered series of causes
definition: A multiplication of causes in which each causes in its own right and its having been caused by the one before is accidental to its causing: a craftsman uses many hammers one after another as each breaks; a man generates as man, not as son of his father. An infinite series of this kind is not impossible (ST I q.46 a.2 ad 7). Not formalized: no premise on a root path is about such series.
